children: By Tom Polansek
Wheat futures extended their fall to a four-week low on the Chicago Board of Trade on Wednesday on expectations that diplomatic efforts could ease Black Sea export disruptions linked to
, analysts said.
Corn and soybean futures also dropped.

Ukraine and Russia, both major grain suppliers, voiced an interest in a limited ceasefire involving grain and energy-related targets, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said after meeting Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov in New York.
Traders said a truce could lead to a recovery in cargo movements that are at a near standstill in the Black Sea, affecting Russian and Ukrainian grain shipments.
Technical selling also weighed on futures, which have pulled back after touching a three-year high this month, analysts said.

"Wheat is the laggard of the grain market, possibly changing its trend from an uptrending market to a downtrend as technical support is being broken," said Brian Hoops, president of Midwest Market Solutions.
Most-active CBOT wheat
closed down 8-3/4 cents at $7.08-1/2 per bushel.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy met US President

on Tuesday and said they discussed a ceasefire on energy-related targets. Still, continued attacks on ports and vessels have tempered expectations among grain traders of a short-term recovery in Black Sea shipping.

"We continue to see little prospect of a near-term normalization in Black Sea export volumes and believe expectations of a durable resolution are premature," said BMI, a Fitch Solutions consulting firm.
Strength in the dollar index
also pressured US grains by making them look more expensive to overseas buyers.

Corn and soybean futures eased after approaching three-year highs this week, with traders waiting to see whether a US-China summit on Thursday boosts Chinese demand for American crops.     China is the world's top soybean importer.
"Pre-negotiations with the Chinese have elicited no indication of any grain deal to be announced," broker Marex said in a note.
CBOT corn
ended down 7-3/4 cents at $5.29 per bushel, while CBOT soybeans
fell 7-1/2 cents to $13.18 per bushel.
